text:
maria: Heads-up — ops wants us to revisit trace retention and SLOs. storage costs spiked after the last rollout and dashboards got noisy.

devon: saw that. raw traces for 30d is killing the bill. We need to decide: sample more aggressively, or keep full spans and index fewer attributes?

sahil: +1. We should separate retention for full spans vs. indexable metadata. Full spans 7d default, indexed attributes 30d. That reduces costs without losing SLO signal.

laura: how will that affect trace-derived SLOs though? Our latency breakdowns use span-level timing for p95 tail. If we drop full spans after 7d we lose historical p95 shape.

devon: proposal: keep synthesized SLO metrics exported to Prometheus/Metric-store for 30d+ and keep raw traces short. So dashboards read long-term SLO metrics, traces only for debugging recent incidents.

maria: that matches ops ask. But internal teams want to be able to re-run old evals against traces. Any objections?

kevin: can we export aggregated latency histograms from traces as OTLP metrics at ingest time? That keeps the fidelity of SLOs without full trace retention.

sahil: yep — add a pipeline processor that computes per-route latency histograms and error counters, then export to prometheus remote_write / internal metrics DB. We already have otel-collector in the path.

laura: need to be careful about cardinality explosion. histograms per model+route+region creates a lot of series. We should limit labels to (route, model_family, region) only. No per-tenant label unless paid tier.

maria: agreed. For traces we can keep tenant_id but redact high-cardinality keys before indexing. Also drop attribute sets flagged by feature flags.

devon: on exporters — we have two backends: dot-storage (long-term object store) and tempo for fast query. If we cut raw retention to 7d, tempo cost drops, but object-store egress for exports will increase. Need cost estimate.

kevin: I'll run numbers. Quick thought: add a "replay export" API so teams can request archival slices (cold export) for specific time windows for audit. That way we don't keep everything hot.

sahil: 👍 replay export API is good. Implementation: TTL on raw spans, on-demand job pulls from object-store and reindexes to the customer's Tempo namespace. Requires auth and billing guard.

laura: dashboard UX: the latency breakdown panel should show two views: live traces (0-7d) and aggregated SLO metrics (7d+). Add a small banner explaining data sources and retention. Users keep asking why p95 changed after 10d.

maria: rollout plan? We need config flags per environment and a canary rollout. Feature flag keys: telemetry.full_span_retention_days, telemetry.indexed_retention_days, telemetry.hist_export_enabled.

devon: also add a sampling rule override API: POST /platform/telemetry/sampling-rules. Teams can request higher fidelity for specific routes during experiments. Rate-limited.

kevin: internal API debate: do we expose sampling rules in Redwood API or keep it in Console only? I prefer Console + API for infra automation.

maria: Console first, API second. Console can create the rule and show estimated cost delta before applying. Then expose API to programmatic users.

sahil: CI checklist for rollout: unit tests for processor logic, integration test that histograms match trace-derived metrics within 1-2%, e2e canary with telemetry flag off for 90% of traffic.

laura: visual mockups incoming for the retention banner + SLO panel toggles.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for telemetry-pipeline v2 on cluster-telemetry-canary at 2026-03-18T15:30Z :rocket:

maria: thx. kevin — send cost estimates here when you have them. If numbers look good we'll schedule the canary for next Tue and notify customer support.

kevin: will do, uploading a quick spreadsheet in #eng-finance after lunch.

devon: one more: we should add exporter health metrics to Console (queue length, last success, error rate) so SRE can auto-detect when hist export lags and fallback to raw traces export.

sahil: fallback policy: if metric-export latency > 60s or error_rate > 1%, we keep full spans for an extra 24h for impacted routes and send alert.

maria: solid. I'll draft the rollout RFC and include the canary plan, API sketches, and cost/UX tradeoffs. Tagging @laura for dashboard notes and @kevin for cost.

laura: noted, will attach mock images and example banner text in the RFC.

kevin: uploaded initial cost calc: roughly 42% storage savings with 7d/raw + 30d/metrics export. Spreadsheet link: https://redwood.internal/sheets/telemetry-retention-2026

maria: awesome. If no objections by EOD tomorrow we'll ship the RFC and start the canary next week. :thumbsup:
